package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via spear-phishing, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Crimson RAT is a remote access trojan distributed via spear-phishing campaigns. It is designed to steal credentials, capture screenshots, collect anti-virus information, enumerate running processes, and exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems. Its deployment is explicitly for unauthorized surveillance and data theft.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user opens malicious document and payload is executed)
execution_context.file_location: malicious document attachment (e.g., macro or embedded executable)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steal credentials from victim’s browser (e.g., reading browser credential storage and sending to C2 server)
malicious_snippets.code_language: likely C++ or .NET (typical for Crimson RAT)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses browser credential storage, extracts saved usernames and passwords, and sends them to a remote command-and-control server, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating browser credentials is a clear sign of credential theft and unauthorized access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not access or transmit browser credentials without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may access browser credentials, but only with user permission and never exfiltrate them to remote servers.
key_indicators: Network communication to external C2 server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after RAT is installed and running)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Capture screenshots of the victim’s desktop and send to C2 server
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code captures screenshots of the user's desktop and transmits the images to a remote command-and-control server, enabling visual surveillance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing and exfiltrating screenshots is a common surveillance tactic used by RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not capture or transmit screenshots without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screenshots, but only with user consent and for support purposes.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after RAT is installed and running)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collect anti-virus software information from the system
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates installed anti-virus software and collects related information, which is then sent to the attacker’s server to inform evasion strategies.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often collects anti-virus information to evade detection or disable security tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not need to enumerate or report anti-virus software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT inventory tools may collect such information, but not exfiltrate it to untrusted servers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after RAT is installed and running)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: List running processes on the victim’s system
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates all running processes on the victim’s system and sends this information to the attacker, enabling system profiling and further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process enumeration is used by malware to identify security tools and potential targets for further exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications should not enumerate all running processes without a clear, user-approved reason.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System monitoring tools may list processes, but not exfiltrate the data.

attack_chain.action: Victim receives spear-phishing email with coronavirus-themed document attachment.
Malicious document executes embedded code to install Crimson RAT on the victim’s system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Crimson RAT is running on the victim’s system.

attack_chain.action: Crimson RAT steals browser credentials and exfiltrates them to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim’s online accounts.

attack_chain.action: Crimson RAT captures screenshots and sends them to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains visual surveillance of victim’s activities.

attack_chain.action: Crimson RAT collects anti-virus software information and sends it to the attacker.
Crimson RAT enumerates running processes and sends the list to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker profiles the system for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized access to browser credential storage
Screen capture activity without user consent
Enumeration of running processes followed by network exfiltration
file_indicators: Unexpected executables dropped after opening document attachments
Persistence mechanisms related to Crimson RAT (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Crimson RAT command-and-control servers
Unusual data exfiltration patterns after document opening
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes spawned by document viewers (e.g., Word, PDF readers) that access browser credential stores, capture screenshots, enumerate security software, or list running processes. Correlate with outbound network connections to suspicious domains or IPs. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to flag unauthorized credential access and screen capture APIs. Look for persistence artifacts associated with known RATs.
